_comment: Audio barge-in MVP cases. Locked 2026-05-30. Each case is ONE Chromium launch with ONE WAV. WAV follows the pad-don't-loop pattern from the fake-mic spike (docs/experiments/2026-05-30-fake-mic-spike/conclusion.md): 5s leading silence + content + 60s trailing silence. The leading silence lets the agent's greeting play; the trailing silence prevents the fake-mic loop from re-feeding the question and confusing the agent's LLM context (verified Spike 3+4 finding).

cases.label: barge-in-true-question
cases.description: Listener asks a coherent question. Pipeline must transcribe + agent must respond. This is the baseline 'does the audio path work end-to-end' case.

cases.label: barge-in-back-channel
cases.description: Listener says 'uh huh' — a back-channel acknowledgement, NOT a real interrupt. A well-tuned barge-in stack should NOT treat this as a turn worthy of agent re-planning. Current Agora-managed default likely WILL trigger a turn — finding that out is the test. Result tells us where we sit vs LiveKit's CNN-based back-channel filter.

expected._note: We deliberately do NOT assert NO-state-change here — the current managed Agora setup almost certainly DOES re-plan on back-channels. The PASS criterion is 'observed and recorded'; the FBR KPI (false-barge-in rate) is the signal we read from this case + B03 across runs.

cases.label: barge-in-silence-only
cases.description: 30s of pure silence (no leading/trailing pattern). VAD MUST NOT trigger a user turn. If it does, FBR is non-zero — a known LiveKit-vs-Agora differentiator and a real customer-experience bug.

expected._note: Silence MUST NOT produce STT events OR agent re-plans. Any deviation is a FBR signal.

cases.label: barge-in-strong-question
cases.description: Real question with strong content — second true-positive case to ensure recall isn't 100% just from B01.

audio_source.text: Why is the old fox so grumpy?

cases.label: barge-in-real-short-intent
cases.description: Short but clear-intent interrupt: 'I disagree'. A tuned filter must NOT mistake this for a back-channel — it's short but the user is making a point.

cases.label: barge-in-true-followup
cases.description: Plain-English clarification request. Should trigger turn cleanly.

cases.label: barge-in-yeah
cases.description: 'Yeah' — single-word back-channel. Default VAD likely triggers; tuned config should suppress.

cases.label: barge-in-okay
cases.description: 'Okay' — common ack that should NOT take the turn.

cases.label: barge-in-noise-cough
cases.description: Short white-noise burst as cough proxy. Pure non-speech — VAD MUST NOT treat as turn.

expected._note: Cough should not be transcribed; if it is, FBR rises.

cases.label: barge-in-noise-tv-background
cases.description: Sustained pink-noise hum as TV-background proxy. Low amplitude, long duration.

expected._note: TV background should not be transcribed; if it is, FBR rises.
